_how: A warning a scanner or Syft logs on every run, reviewed and expected (docs/decisions/0011-vulnerability-scanners.md). packaging/container/tool_warnings.py lists a matching warning as expected instead of raising it on the run: the tool, text found in the warning, why it is expected, who reviewed it, and when the review expires (YYYY-MM-DD, at most 90 days out). An expired entry raises its warning again, so each one gets looked at again.

warnings.reason: Upstream Trivy doesn't recognize Red Hat Hardened Images' operating system (Hummingbird) and has no advisories for it, so it checks only language packages and secrets. Grype covers the OS packages; vuln_gate.py records each scanner's coverage and needs a review if none covers them.

warnings.text: trivy has no advisory data for this image's operating system (not recognized)
warnings.reason: The same gap, as vuln_gate.py records it: upstream Trivy doesn't recognize Hummingbird. Grype's data covers it. A scanner that recognizes the OS but has no data for it, as Red Hat's build of Trivy does, isn't matched by this entry and is raised.

warnings.text: Third-party SBOM may lead to inaccurate vulnerability detection
warnings.reason: Trivy reads any SBOM file it finds in an image as a list of packages. The runtime base has two that come with pip: dist-info/sboms/rpm.cdx.json (from Red Hat's RPM build) and pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json (pip's vendored libraries). The Containerfile removes pip in a later layer, but Trivy reads each layer before deletions, so it still sees them. They change no finding: Trivy's only language package is wd2l's own (#236).

warnings.text: Using severities from other vendors for some vulnerabilities
warnings.reason: On UBI 9 (the comparison image), Red Hat gives some vulnerabilities no severity of its own, and Trivy then uses another source's rating, as its documentation describes. The rating Trivy reports is the one each summary shows.

warnings.text: Recommend using Trivy to generate SBOMs
warnings.reason: The other half of the same event: Trivy logs this line with the one above whenever it reads an SBOM it didn't make, here pip's two in the base layer. It never sees wd2l's own SBOMs, which Syft makes for the release (docs/decisions/0010-sbom-generator.md) (#236).
